account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments, though the mill grain inspection was incomplete: I could not locate the miller or obtain stock records, so I have no findings about supplies or storage. The secretary has secured my report and is seeking a follow-up tomorrow at ten, subject to my appointments and the miller's confirmation. No council letters or urgent council decisions had reached the secretary this afternoon.

The notable extra business is an eighteen hundred lighting inspection at the town hall. The baker said freight had told him about it, and I confirmed it; the secretary also says it remains arranged. The baker reports eighty contracted loaves delivered to the hall, with freight confirming delivery to him. These preparations suggest some planned hall use, but I have not learned its purpose, inspected the lights, or personally checked the bread delivery. I should not assume more.

I visited my retired neighbour at the dockside cottage for tea. They described a peaceful afternoon and offered to accompany me to the lighting inspection. The secretary also came to the cottage to discuss the mill follow-up. I am now back in my office with the secretary nearby, after returning for the sixteen thirty office appointment; it is seventeen hundred. I should hear any outstanding office business before the inspection and my nineteen hundred return home. The earlier rumour about bridge or port changes remains unconfirmed: the secretary's written brief said no actual proposal had been received.
